text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes is diagnosed using specific blood tests that measure your blood sugar levels.
snippet_highlighted_words: using specific blood tests that measure your blood sugar levels

text_blocks.snippet: According to the American Diabetes Association, doctors use these main blood tests for a diagnosis:

list.snippet: A1C Test: Measures your average blood sugar over the past two to three months. A result of 6.5% or higher on two separate tests means you have diabetes. No fasting is required.
Fasting Plasma Glucose (FPG) Test: Measures your blood sugar after you do not eat or drink anything except water for at least eight hours. A result of 126 mg/dL or higher means you have diabetes.
Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT): Measures your blood sugar two hours after you drink a special sweet liquid. A level of 200 mg/dL or higher confirms diabetes.
Random Plasma Glucose Test: Checks your blood sugar at any time when you have severe diabetes symptoms. A level of 200 mg/dL or higher indicates diabetes.

text_blocks.snippet: Doctors usually repeat an abnormal test on a second day to confirm the diagnosis, unless you have very high blood sugar or clear, classic symptoms.
